by_task.when: Wisconsin exemptions are allowable and an asset qualifies as personal-use consumer goods under Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(d) or as a motor vehicle under § 815.18(3)(g).
by_task.procedure: Report one asset-level amount without dividing jointly owned value into spouse shares. For consumer goods, use the lesser of asset value and $12,000 for one debtor or $24,000 for two joint debtors. For a motor vehicle, start with $4,000 per debtor and add unused § 815.18(3)(d) capacity when the facts state no consumption, never exceeding asset value.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not infer business use, halve an asset merely because ownership is joint, or transfer unused consumer-goods capacity to property other than a motor vehicle.

operations.rationale: Source 245 EV shows the parent halving jointly owned consumer-property values despite § 815.18(8), while source 227 EV shows omission of the expressly available unused-consumer-goods increase for a motor vehicle. This EV-only skill corrects those amount rules without changing the already-correct eligibility classifications.
